claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A physics-informed transformer can integrate reduced-order physics simulations with targeted experimental fracture data.
The proposed framework can embed priors concerning dislocation mobility, energy barriers, and fracture-initiation criteria in its architecture.
The hierarchical heterostructure's chemical fluctuations and local deformation mechanisms govern elastic properties.
The hierarchical heterostructure's chemical fluctuations and local deformation mechanisms govern fracture properties.
Transformer self-attention captures complex microstructural descriptors and their interactions.
Embedded physics constraints guide predictions to reflect stress concentrations.
Embedded physics constraints guide predictions to reflect dislocation dynamics.
Embedded physics constraints guide predictions to reflect fracture phenomena.
The proposed method will reduce RMSE for Young's-modulus predictions by approximately 20–30% relative to the baseline methods.
The proposed method will reduce RMSE for yield-strength predictions by approximately 20–30% relative to the baseline methods.
The proposed method will reduce RMSE for toughness predictions by approximately 20–30% relative to the baseline methods.
The proposed method will be up to ten times faster than the established baseline methods.
Direct thermophysical calculations, CALPHAD, first-principles simulations, and conventional machine learning have high computational demands.
Existing baseline methods have low predictive reliability for fracture properties.
The method will become unreliable when its training data inadequately sample hierarchical microstructural variability.
The method will become unreliable when testing conditions fall outside the validity regime of its embedded dislocation and fracture-mechanics assumptions.
The magnitude of the accuracy and efficiency gains depends on the fidelity and representativeness of the training data and the robustness of the physics priors.
